sentences.text: WOMAN: Good morning. I'm doing a survey of shoppers in Broadbeach. Would you have a few minutes to spare to answer some questions?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 早上好。我正在Broadbeach开展一项购物者调查。您能否抽出几分钟时间回答几个问题？

sentences.text: MAN: Oh... erm... yes, I guess that would be ok.
sentences.zh: MAN: 哦……嗯……是的，我想这应该没问题。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Thank you very much. Everybody seems so busy today.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 非常感谢。今天看起来每个人都很忙。

sentences.text: MAN: Well actually I don't have loads of time, so...
sentences.zh: MAN: 其实我并没有太多时间，所以……

sentences.text: WOMAN: Oh yes, of course. It really won't take long. Could I start by taking your name please?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 哦，是的，当然可以。真的不会花太久。我可以先记下您的姓名吗？

sentences.text: MAN: Martyn Leigh. Martyn's with a Y.
sentences.zh: MAN: 马丁·利思。‘马丁’的拼写中用的是字母Y。

sentences.text: WOMAN: And is your family name spelt L-double-E?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 您的姓氏拼写是L-双E吗？

sentences.text: MAN: It's L-E-1-G-H.
sentences.zh: MAN: 是L-E-I-G-H。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Thank you. We don't actually publish your name or details. It just makes it easier for me to identify people when I look at all the results at the end.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 谢谢。实际上我们并不会公开您的姓名或个人信息，只是在最后汇总所有调查结果时，便于我识别不同受访者。

sentences.text: MAN: I see.
sentences.zh: MAN: 明白了。

sentences.text: WOMAN: And can I ask, how did you get into town today?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 还想请问一下，您今天是怎么来镇上的？

sentences.text: MAN: Well, normally I catch the bus, but I'm on my motorbike today because I'm going to work later.
sentences.zh: MAN: 通常我乘公交车，但今天骑了我的摩托车，因为稍后我要去上班。

sentences.text: WOMAN: And could you tell me what you're doing this morning, I mean, the reason for your trip into town?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 您能告诉我您今天上午来镇上的目的吗？也就是说，您这次进城的原因是什么？

sentences.text: MAN: I've just been to the hairdresser. You see, I have a job interview at the council in a few days.
sentences.zh: MAN: 我刚去理了发。您知道，几天后我要去市政厅参加一场工作面试。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Oh really! Well, good luck with that.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 哦，真的吗！祝您面试顺利！

sentences.text: MAN: Thanks a lot. And now I'm on my way to buy a suit that I can wear to the interview. I don't actually own one at the moment!
sentences.zh: MAN: 非常感谢！接下来我要去买一套面试时穿的西装——目前我手头还没有一套呢！

sentences.text: WOMAN: OK. Is that everything you're planning to do in town?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 好的。您今天在镇上就只计划做这些事吗？

sentences.text: MAN: Yeah. Well, I've got to go and pick up my @m.QR. It broke a couple of days ago so I took it to the shop to get it fixed. They had to order a spare part, but apparently it's ready for collection now. I can't wait to get it back.
sentences.zh: MAN: 是的。不过我还得去取回我的@ m.QR。它几天前坏了，所以我送去店里维修；他们需要订购一个备用零件，但据说现在已修好、可以取回了。我真迫不及待想拿回来！

sentences.text: WOMAN: I'm sure. I hate it when my technology breaks down.... One more thing, it's Saturday today - is that when you like to do your shopping?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 我完全理解。我的电子设备出故障时也特别烦人……还有一件事：今天是星期六——您通常喜欢选在周六购物吗？

sentences.text: MAN: Well it's more a question of when I'm free. If I'm free on a Monday. that's when I choose to come into town. The shops are less busy then, which I always prefer.
sentences.zh: MAN: 其实更多取决于我什么时候有空。如果周一有空，我就会选择那天进城购物。那时商店人比较少，我向来更喜欢这样。

sentences.text: WOMAN: So, I'd like to ask you a few more questions to get your views about shopping in Broadbeach, if that's ok.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那么，我想再问您几个问题，了解您对布罗德比奇购物的看法，可以吗？

sentences.text: MAN: Sure. What would you like to know specifically?
sentences.zh: MAN: 当然可以。您具体想了解些什么？

sentences.text: WOMAN: What would you say you like best about the shops here?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 您觉得这里商店最吸引您的地方是什么？

sentences.text: MAN: I'd probably say it's the service you get wherever you go.
sentences.zh: MAN: 我大概会说是无论去哪家店都能享受到的优质服务。

sentences.text: WOMAN: OK. And what do you think about the range of shops in Broadbeach?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 好的。那么，您如何看待布罗德比奇的商铺种类？

sentences.text: MAN: Oh you can get almost anything you want here.
sentences.zh: MAN: 哦，您在这里几乎能买到任何想要的东西。

sentences.text: WOMAN: And what about recent changes? What do you like and dislike about them? For example, there are a lot of new coffee shops now, are you enjoying them?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那么最近的变化呢？您喜欢和不喜欢哪些方面？例如，现在新增了许多咖啡馆，您喜欢它们吗？

sentences.text: MAN: No, there are too many of them. It's a shame as those places could be occupied by other kinds of shops.
sentences.zh: MAN: 不喜欢，咖啡馆实在太多了。这很可惜，因为这些店面本可以留给其他类型的商店。

sentences.text: WOMAN: What would you like to see instead?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那您希望看到什么替代方案呢？

sentences.text: MAN: Well, I think we have enough clothing shops. But there's only one place that sells books at the moment. It'd be nice to have a choice, you know.
sentences.zh: MAN: 嗯，我觉得目前服装店已经够多了。但眼下只有一家书店。要是能有更多选择就更好了，您知道吧。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Right. And have you been to the new shopping centre outside Broadbeach yet, Martyn?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 明白了。马丁，您去过布罗德比奇外面那座新建的购物中心了吗？

sentences.text: MAN: Yes, once or twice. It's not that far from where I live.
sentences.zh: MAN: 去过一两次。它离我家并不远。

sentences.text: WOMAN: It's a very modern-looking building, isn't it?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那是一座外观非常现代的建筑，对吧？

sentences.text: MAN: Yes, and it's lovely. The glass roof is certainly impressive. But my favourite thing is the plants they've put around the building. They're amazing, and so big already.
sentences.zh: MAN: 是的，而且很漂亮。玻璃屋顶确实令人印象深刻。但我最喜欢的是环绕建筑布置的那些植物——它们太惊艳了，而且长得已经很大了。

sentences.text: WOMAN: And what about the entertainment facilities? Have you used any of them yet?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那娱乐设施呢？您用过其中任何一项吗？

sentences.text: MAN: Like the new cinema?
sentences.zh: MAN: 比如那家新电影院？

sentences.text: WOMAN: Nah, not yet. I can't see any advantage in having it there because the one in town is actually bigger.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 不，还没去过。我觉得建在那里没什么优势，因为镇上的那家电影院实际上更大。

sentences.text: OK, well thank you so much for...
sentences.zh: OK，那么非常感谢您……

sentences.text: Hello and welcome to this podcast telling you about our annual business exhibition. This year, as always, it will be full of the very best speakers, features and innovations.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听本期播客，为您介绍我们的年度商业展览。今年，一如往常，展会将汇聚最优秀的演讲嘉宾、精彩特色活动及前沿创新成果。

sentences.text: Let me start by reading some feedback from James Craig, who's exhibited with us for the past two years. James says, 'I'm director of a company called TalkCon, which is an office phone system. The first year we exhibited, we had a stand in the Business Village, where we made a lot of useful contacts. We also used the Breakout area where people could sit down and relax. and try out our products. and due to popular request we used that again last year. Last year we also sponsored the innovative Business Connections Zone where people could leave their contact details on a board to contact other companies, and that also effectively raised our corporate profile. We"re hoping that in the coming exhibition we'll also have a presence in the Digital Marketing centre, which is clearly a key area for our company. And also maybe have our own Talkcon Zone, at some stage.' The exhibition's open from 8am to 11 pm and there's a range of special events for you to enjoy in the evening.
sentences.zh: 让我先朗读一下詹姆斯·克雷格（James Craig）的反馈意见，他已连续两年参加我们的展会。詹姆斯表示：'我是名为TalkCon公司的总监，我们主营办公电话系统。第一年参展时，我们在商务村设有展位，借此结识了许多有价值的合作伙伴。我们还利用了“ breakout”休息区——人们可以在此坐下放松并试用我们的产品；由于反响热烈，去年我们再次使用了该区域。去年，我们还赞助了富有创意的“商务联络区”，参会者可将联系方式留在展板上，以便与其他公司取得联系，此举也有效提升了我们公司的企业形象。我们希望在即将举办的展会中，也能入驻数字营销中心——这显然是我们公司的一个关键领域；此外，或许还能在某个阶段设立专属的TalkCon专区。' 展会开放时间为上午8点至晚上11点，晚间还将为您呈现一系列精彩特别活动。

sentences.text: As well as a unique chance to publicise your company, businesses who exhibit with us can claim discounts on a number of popular brands, including major high street fashion and jewellery outlets. as well as grocery chains. Discounts available range from 3.5% up to an amazing 15%, so you can save a lot of money. In fact, the average saving made by each exhibitor came to over £400! The scheme is available to every member of your organisation so this is a benefit that really does have something for you all.
sentences.zh: 除提供独一无二的企业宣传机会外，参展企业还可享受多个热门品牌的折扣优惠，涵盖主流街头时尚与珠宝门店，以及大型连锁超市。折扣幅度从3.5%至高达15%不等，助您节省大量开支。事实上，每位参展商平均节省金额超过400英镑！该优惠计划面向贵组织全体成员开放，因此这是一项真正惠及全员的福利。

sentences.text: Now let me tell you about some of our keynote speakers for this year's exhibition.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我为您介绍本届展会的部分主旨演讲嘉宾。

sentences.text: Jim Clowrie started off selling vegetables from a small plot, then opened a small café.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·克洛里（Jim Clowrie）最初在一小块土地上销售蔬菜，随后开设了一家小型咖啡馆。

sentences.text: Rather to his surprise this became a bit of a sensation, and in a remarkably short time he had opened an amazing 76 restaurants worldwide. He'll be telling you how it all happened, and how it changed his life.
sentences.zh: 令他颇感意外的是，这家咖啡馆竟迅速走红；短短时间内，他便在全球成功开设了76家餐厅。他将向您讲述这一切是如何发生的，以及这一经历如何改变了他的人生。

sentences.text: David France will be giving an inspirational talk about how as a business-minded teenager he managed to set up his own company, and even to be the first person under 18 to get a business bank account. David's company has gone from strength to strength but he isn't just interested in making money - he also makes regular donations to organisations helping those in need both in the UK and elsewhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 大卫·弗朗斯（David France）将带来一场鼓舞人心的演讲，讲述他作为一名具有商业头脑的青少年，如何创办了自己的公司，甚至成为英国首位未满18岁即成功开设企业银行账户的人。大卫的公司持续发展壮大，但他不仅关注盈利——他还定期向援助英国及世界各地弱势群体的各类组织捐款。

sentences.text: 011/12 011/12 013/14 013/14 Oliver Stanton was born and educated in the UK, and then went to Malaysia where he set up a rubber-wood furniture business. He then built log houses in the mountains in Japan before moving to Hong Kong to set up a digital marketing business. After that he moved back to the UK with his wife Saiphin, and together they opened a Thai café. He'll be telling you about what he discovered during his travels around the world about business practices in different cultures.
sentences.zh: 奥利弗·斯坦顿（Oliver Stanton）出生于英国并在英国接受教育，之后前往马来西亚创办了一家橡胶木家具企业；随后又在日本山区建造原木房屋；继而移居香港创立一家数字营销公司；此后携妻子赛芬（Saiphin）返回英国，共同开设了一家泰国风味咖啡馆。他将在演讲中分享自己环游世界期间，在不同文化背景下所观察到的商业实践及其启示。

sentences.text: Francesca Heptonstall is a broadcaster and businesswoman who's known for her down­ to-earth attitude. After winning a top job in a TV contest, she launched a number of online deal sites. Her main business interest is in technology, but she's also passionate about helping people gain employment and organises an annual jobs fair, so she'll be concentrating on this in her talk.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯卡·赫普顿斯塔尔（Francesca Heptonstall）是一位广播主持人兼企业家，以务实亲和的风格著称。她在一场电视竞赛中赢得重要职位后，创办了多家线上优惠信息网站。她主要专注于科技领域，同时也热衷于帮助人们实现就业，并每年组织一场就业博览会；因此，她的演讲将聚焦于这一主题。

sentences.text: Salman Khan is the Chief Executive of OBF Enterprises, and has turned around this business from a major publishing business to one of the UK's largest digital marketing service providers. He'll be talking about the need for flexibility to cope with new directions in 9 today's business world.
sentences.zh: 萨尔曼·汗（Salman Khan）是OBF企业集团首席执行官，成功将该公司由一家大型出版企业转型为英国最大的数字营销服务提供商之一。他将围绕当今商业世界中应对新发展方向所需的灵活性展开演讲。

sentences.text: Finally, Annie Craven is a consultant and coach who works with people to create lasting changes in their business and life. Her session will offer an interactive look at different obstacles in people's own lives, not just in business. She also looks at how you can overcome them, whether you're starting out in business or at the top of your game.
sentences.zh: 最后，安妮·克雷文（Annie Craven）是一位顾问兼教练，致力于协助人们在其事业与生活中实现持久改变。她的工作坊将以互动方式探讨人们生活中（不仅限于商业领域）所面临的各类障碍，并指导您如何克服这些挑战——无论您是创业新手，还是行业翘楚。

sentences.text: Now let me...
sentences.zh: 现在，让我……

sentences.text: MIA: You know that joint presentation we've got to do this semester, Leo?
sentences.zh: MIA: 你知道我们这学期要做的那个联合报告吗，Leo？

sentences.text: LEO: On houses of the future?
sentences.zh: LEO: 关于未来住宅的？

sentences.text: MIA: That's right. I'm a bit concerned - are we meant to come up with creative new suggestions for these houses?
sentences.zh: MIA: 没错。我有点担心——我们是不是得为这些住宅提出富有创意的新建议？

sentences.text: LEO: I don't think so. It's more a matter of reporting and evaluating possible developments. But we mustn't be too general. we've got to support our points by referring to specific cases. So that'll need a lot of work.
sentences.zh: LEO: 我觉得没必要。这更多是关于汇报和评估可能的发展趋势。但我们不能太笼统，必须通过引用具体案例来支撑我们的观点。因此这需要大量工作。

sentences.text: MIA: I'm afraid so. When's it got to be done by?
sentences.zh: MIA: 恐怕确实如此。这个报告什么时候要交？

sentences.text: LEO: In about 6 weeks, so that's not too much of a rush.
sentences.zh: LEO: 大约六周后，所以时间上还不算太紧张。

sentences.text: MIA: Good. We'd better decide now what type of housing we're going to focus on.
sentences.zh: MIA: 太好了。我们最好现在就决定聚焦哪一类住宅。

sentences.text: LEO: How about housing for different generations living together?
sentences.zh: LEO: 共同居住的多代际住宅怎么样？

sentences.text: MIA: We could do. Or accommodation for one person?
sentences.zh: MIA: 我们也可以选这个。或者单人住所呢？

sentences.text: LEO: I think someone else is doing that. I was wondering about housing for the elderly? That's likely to become more important.
sentences.zh: LEO: 我觉得别人已经在做单人住所了。我在想老年人住宅如何？这方面的重要性可能会日益提升。

sentences.text: MIA: Yeah that's true. But I think your suggestion about intergenerational living might be more interesting - let's go with that.
sentences.zh: MIA: 是啊，的确如此。不过我觉得你提出的多代际共居方案可能更有趣——我们就选这个吧。

sentences.text: LEO: OK. Now I think the future demand is mainly going to be for accommodation in urban areas. So one way of meeting that demand might be to use existing commercial buildings and adapt them to form accommodation...
sentences.zh: LEO: 好的。我认为未来的主要需求将集中在城市地区的住宅上。因此，满足这一需求的一种方式可能是改造现有的商业建筑，使其转变为住宅……

sentences.text: MIA: ... or come up with original ways of organising space so that people can live in smaller homes. But I think the solution is to design multi-storey apartment blocks.
sentences.zh: MIA: ……或者创新性地规划空间，使人们能在更小的住宅中生活。但我认为解决方案是设计多层公寓楼。

sentences.text: LEO: Building up rather than out. yes.
sentences.zh: LEO: 向上建造而非向外扩展，没错。

sentences.text: MIA: Let's think of some specific developments for houses of the future.
sentences.zh: MIA: 我们来想想一些未来住宅的具体发展方案吧。

sentences.text: LEO: OK. How about increased use of roof space on high-rise buildings for gardens.
sentences.zh: LEO: 好的。比如在高层建筑屋顶上更多地开辟花园空间如何？

sentences.text: MIA: Yes. In fact it doesn't have to be high-rise, you can do it on a one-storey building in a suburb, but it would greatly improve how you feel if you live in an urban high-rise.
sentences.zh: MIA: 对。事实上，不一定非得是高层建筑，郊区的单层建筑也可以这么做；但若应用于城市高层住宅，则会极大改善住户的心理感受。

sentences.text: LEO: Especially if you don't have a balcony.
sentences.zh: LEO: 尤其是住户没有阳台的情况下。

sentences.text: MIA: Yes. I think homes of the future will all need access to a shared working space, somewhere in the same building or group of houses, where people can go and work instead of just having a laptop on the kitchen table.
sentences.zh: MIA: 是的。我认为未来的住宅都应配备共享工作空间——就在同一栋楼或同一住宅群内，供住户前往办公，而不只是把笔记本电脑放在厨房餐桌上。

sentences.text: LEO: Yes, so they aren't having to travel to an office but can still interact with others.
sentences.zh: LEO: 没错，这样他们就不必前往办公室通勤，却仍能与他人互动。

sentences.text: MIA: That's often how new ideas get generated - by chatting to someone from a different profession.
sentences.zh: MIA: 新想法往往就是这样产生的——通过与不同职业的人聊天。

sentences.text: LEO: Yeah. I read about a type of design where the internal walls of an apartment are moveable, so the space can be adapted over time as people's needs change.
sentences.zh: LEO: 是的。我读到过一种设计，公寓内部的墙壁是可以移动的，因此空间可以根据人们需求的变化而随时间调整。

sentences.text: MIA: Like when children leave school and start working but still continue to live with their parents for many years? Or when an elderly relative moves in with the family... it would mean they could still have their own space. specially designed for their needs.
sentences.zh: MIA: 比如孩子毕业开始工作后仍长期与父母同住？又或者年迈的亲戚搬来与家人同住……这样他们仍能拥有自己专属的空间，且该空间会特别根据他们的需求进行设计。

sentences.text: LEO: Yes. Have you heard about those smart bathroom mirrors which can monitor people's health? They recognise signs of illness and contact a doctor automatically?
sentences.zh: LEO: 是的。你听说过那种智能浴室镜子吗？它能监测人们的健康状况，识别疾病征兆并自动联系医生？

sentences.text: MIA: Hmm, not so sure they're a good idea.
sentences.zh: MIA: 嗯，我不太确定这是否是个好主意。

sentences.text: LEO: Nor am I. People might worry about conditions which aren't serious at all.
sentences.zh: LEO: 我也不这么认为。人们可能会为根本并不严重的健康状况而担忧。

sentences.text: MIA: What about transport? Wouldn't it be good if there were bike sheds with charging points, so people could store their electric bikes securely and charge them up at the same time.
sentences.zh: MIA: 那交通方面呢？如果自行车棚配备充电设施，人们就能安全存放电动自行车，同时为其充电，这难道不是很好吗？

sentences.text: LEO: Yes. That would encourage more people to cycle. instead of using their car.
sentences.zh: LEO: 是的。这将鼓励更多人骑自行车，而不是开车。

sentences.text: MIA: Much better for the planet.
sentences.zh: MIA: 对地球环境要友好得多。

sentences.text: LEO: I read about one housing development where cars had to be left just outside it, so the centre was all a pedestrianised area. Great for families with children.
sentences.zh: LEO: 我读到过一个住宅开发项目，要求汽车必须停放在小区外围，因此整个中心区域都是步行区。这对有孩子的家庭来说非常理想。

sentences.text: MIA: Maybe. But what if you're disabled or elderly. and can"t walk far? It wouldn't be so good for people like that.
sentences.zh: MIA: 或许吧。但如果有人残疾或年迈，无法长距离步行呢？对这类人群而言，这种设计就不太友好了。

sentences.text: LEO: No.
sentences.zh: LEO: 的确如此。

sentences.text: I saw a scheme for communal vegetable plots, where neighbours could decide what to grow together. That"d be a great way for older people to get to know one another, especially if they're no longer going out to work.
sentences.zh: 我看到过一个社区菜园计划，邻居们可以共同决定一起种植什么作物。这对老年人来说是彼此相识的好方式，尤其当他们已不再外出工作时。

sentences.text: Yes, doing something together's always more enjoyable, isn't it? Do you think...
sentences.zh: 是的，一起做事总是更愉快，不是吗？你觉得……

sentences.text: Today's lecture is about studies that look at how music therapy can be used to help patients who undergo surgery. Now, most people undergo a surgical procedure at some point in their lives. And more than fifty-one million operations are performed annually in the USA.
sentences.zh: 今天的讲座主题是探讨音乐治疗如何帮助接受手术的患者。目前，大多数人在一生中都会经历某种外科手术。仅在美国，每年就进行超过五千一百万例手术。

sentences.text: But there's no escaping the fact that most patients feel uncomfortable following surgery.
sentences.zh: 但不可否认的是，大多数患者在术后都会感到不适。

sentences.text: They may have difficulty mobilising, and even sitting up in bed can feel too much. They may also be negatively affected by having their routine disturbed, you know, like if they can't do the things they normally do, or have to devote a lot of time to appointments such as physiotherapy, to aid their recovery.
sentences.zh: 他们可能难以活动，甚至在床上坐起来都感觉十分吃力。此外，日常作息被打乱也会对他们产生负面影响，比如无法照常进行日常活动，或不得不花费大量时间前往物理治疗等复健预约。

sentences.text: Currently. the main strategy for improving recovery is medication to control pain, and this can be administered to patients in the short, medium or longer term, depending on the extent of their surgery. But music is still not an everyday part of the post-surgical phase. despite a wealth of relevant studies supporting its potential in recovery.
sentences.zh: 目前，改善术后康复的主要策略是使用止痛药物，这些药物可根据手术范围的大小，在短期、中期或更长时间内给予患者。然而，尽管已有大量相关研究支持音乐在康复过程中的潜在作用，音乐仍未成为术后常规护理的一部分。

sentences.text: Earlier this year, a research team set out to assess all the available evidence so that they could highlight the potential for music in surgical recovery. They identified nearly a hundred trials involving a total of seven thousand patients who were played recorded music as part of their post-operative care. The researchers then looked at what impact the music had on the patients. They discovered that patients who had been played music reported feeling happier and more satisfied in the post-operative phase, and the length of their stay was shorter than for patients who had not listened to any music.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，一支研究团队着手全面评估所有现有证据，以凸显音乐在术后康复中的潜力。他们共识别出近一百项临床试验，涉及总计七千名患者；这些患者在术后护理期间均接受了录音音乐干预。随后，研究人员考察了音乐对患者产生的影响。他们发现，聆听音乐的患者在术后阶段报告心情更愉悦、满意度更高，且住院时间比未听音乐的患者更短。

sentences.text: The researchers also explored the patients' choice of music, and their findings showed that a wide variety of music styles was evident. However, a common factor was that the chosen music had a calming quality. Some of the patients listened to music with headphones, but it was quiet enough not to prevent them from being able to communicate with nurses and other staff. More often though, the mode of delivery was by what are known as music pillows. These broadcast sound that is only audible to the person lying on them. The research involved testing music before, during or after operations or a combination. Some patients listened to the music just once a day, while others had several episodes a day.
sentences.zh: 研究人员还调查了患者对音乐类型的选择，结果表明所选音乐风格极为多样。但一个共同特点是：所选音乐普遍具有舒缓 calming 的特质。部分患者通过耳机听音乐，音量足够轻柔，不会妨碍其与护士及其他医护人员交流。但更常见的播放方式是使用所谓‘音乐枕’——这种枕头仅使躺在上面的人能听到所播放的声音。研究涵盖术前、术中、术后单独或联合播放音乐的情形。有些患者每天只听一次音乐，而另一些人则每天多次聆听。

sentences.text: When asked to report their experience of listening to music, surgical patients said that either they had no feelings of anxiety at any point, or those feelings were only slight.
sentences.zh: 当被要求报告听音乐的体验时，外科患者表示，要么全程毫无焦虑感，要么仅有轻微焦虑感。

sentences.text: Patients who hadn't listened to music, on the other hand, reported higher levels of dissatisfaction. This feedback from all of the patients was then cross-checked against their medical notes. And in every case, those who were given music to listen to didn't need as much medication to ease their pain as those patients who weren't played music. The type of music, patient choice and timing, before, during or after the surgery didn't make much difference. And it even worked when patients were played music under general anaesthetic, although the positive effects were greater when patients were awake.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，未听音乐的患者报告了更高程度的不满。研究人员将所有患者的反馈与其病历记录交叉核对，结果发现：所有听过音乐的患者，所需止痛药剂量均少于未听音乐的患者。音乐类型、患者自主选择以及播放时机（术前、术中或术后）均未产生显著差异；即便在全身麻醉状态下播放音乐也有效果，不过当患者处于清醒状态时，积极效应更为明显。

sentences.text: All the evidence suggests that music has a positive effect on post-operative patients, but it's not entirely clear how or why this is the case. A lot of people listen to music in daily life as a way to relax and forget their problems, but the researchers came to the conclusion that it worked on patients by distraction. I suppose it was something familiar and gave them something they could control.
sentences.zh: 所有证据均表明，音乐对术后患者具有积极影响，但其具体作用机制及原因尚不完全明确。许多人日常生活中听音乐是为了放松并暂时忘却烦恼，但研究人员最终得出结论：音乐主要通过‘分散注意力’的方式起效。我想，这或许是因为音乐令人熟悉，且赋予患者一种可控感。

sentences.text: The researchers say there is now sufficient research to demonstrate that music should be available to all patients undergoing operations. They say patients should be able to choose what they'd like to listen to, and if they prefer, recordings taken from nature can be just as good as music. Surgical teams may prefer patients to listen to music before the procedure or as soon as they arrive back onto the ward. Clearly, there's more to learn about this area, and the team now plan to focus their next research on the most appropriate volume to play the music at. And I look forward to reading the results of their study.
sentences.zh: 研究人员指出，目前已有充分的研究证据表明，音乐理应向所有接受手术的患者开放提供。他们建议患者应能自主选择想听的内容，若患者偏好，来自大自然的录音效果亦可与音乐相当。外科团队可能更倾向于让患者在手术前或刚返回病房时即开始听音乐。显然，该领域仍有诸多待探索之处，研究团队下一步计划聚焦于确定播放音乐的最适宜音量。我期待阅读他们后续研究的结果。

sentences.text: It will be interesting to see...
sentences.zh: 这将非常有趣……
